name: Nominal
summary: Nominal develops AI-enabled accounting and financial-operations software for mid-market and enterprise finance teams.
overview: Nominal provides an accounting and financial-operations platform designed to automate close, reporting, and related workflows. The company announced a $20 million Series A in July 2025; the financing valuation was not disclosed.

facts.label: Latest financing
facts.note: Nominal announced a $20 million Series A; its valuation was not disclosed.

bull_case: Finance teams have clear incentives to reduce manual close and reporting work, and automation can compound as a customer adds entities and workflows.
bear_case: Accounting software faces high switching costs, long implementation cycles, and entrenched ERP and close-management competitors.
directory_notes: Public financing and operating data remain limited.

intelligence.description: AI-enabled accounting and financial-operations software for modern finance teams.

metrics.label: Latest valuation
metrics.note: Valuation was not announced with the Series A

company: Nominal sells a financial-operations platform focused on making accounting, close, and reporting workflows more automated. The company positions its product for finance teams that need to manage increasing complexity without expanding manual processes at the same rate.
In July 2025, Nominal announced a $20 million Series A. The company disclosed the round but not a valuation, so this profile does not treat the financing as a priced valuation event.
intelligence.why_it_matters: Financial workflow software is a practical testing ground for AI adoption because the buyer already measures speed, accuracy, and control. Nominal is relevant to the private-market software stack competing for the finance office's system of record.

changed.text: Nominal announced a $20M Series A; the round's valuation was not disclosed.

takeaways: The July 2025 Series A is the profile's latest disclosed funding event.
Automation of close and reporting is the central product thesis.
ERP incumbency and implementation risk remain meaningful constraints.
